content.text:
Googlebook is raising the bar for premium laptops: Google's September 21 post describes five launch models and says buyers can choose Intel Core Ultra Series 3 or Snapdragon X Elite processors. This establishes a multi-silicon lineup rather than an Intel-exclusive platform. (time=2026-09-21; cutoff=BEFORE_CUTOFF).
New ASUS Googlebook 14 Available for Pre-Order: ASUS's September 21 announcement identifies its Googlebook 14 with an Intel Core Ultra 5 325 processor and says U.S. preorders are open. Thus, one named Intel-powered model was publicly specified before the September 22 Yahoo/Zacks coverage. (time=2026-09-21; cutoff=BEFORE_CUTOFF).
The first Googlebook devices surface with Intel, Snapdragon: The June report described early Googlebook device codenames associated with Intel, Snapdragon, and MediaTek platforms, while noting that which models would launch and when was unclear. It provides context for the later named Intel OEM lineup, not evidence of production commitments. (time=2026-06-04T08:35:00-07:00; cutoff=BEFORE_CUTOFF).

content.text:

It does not report actual deliveries or sales. (time=2026-09-21; cutoff=BEFORE_CUTOFF).
Can Intel's Core Ultra Expansion With Googlebook Benefit the Stock?: The article repeats Intel's announcement that Acer, ASUS, and Lenovo would bring out Core Ultra Series 3 Googlebooks and discusses competing PC processors. It adds no reported unit volume, confirmed sell-through, production order, or repeat order in the captured text. (time=2026-09-22T15:22:00Z; cutoff=BEFORE_CUTOFF).
